title: Graduate Engineer - Mechanical New Technology
description: Are you passionate about building a strong foundation in engineering design and technology? Do you enjoy learning from experienced engineers while contributing to real‑world oilfield engineering solutions? Join our team Baker Hughes is a global energy‑technology company operating in over 120 countries. We deliver innovative solutions that make energy safer, cleaner, and more efficient. Our engineering teams play a vital role in designing and delivering oilfield subsurface components, systems, and control equipment that enable reliable energy production worldwide. Partner with the best As an Engineer, Graduate , you will support the design and development of oilfield subsurface components, systems, and/or controls equipment. You will work under the close guidance of a Lead Engineer and designated Mentors , gaining hands‑on experience while contributing to engineering activities in line with company standards, competence frameworks, and work instructions. This role provides a structured environment to develop your technical, professional, and safety competencies while supporting design, manufacturing, and verification activities. As an Engineer, Graduate you will be responsible for: Supporting the creation of layouts, functional component specifications, stack‑up evaluations, and assembly procedures Interpreting customer engineering specifications to produce layout, detail, and assembly designs Assisting with the creation of work packs, reviewing detail drawings, and supporting small engineering teams under supervision Developing conceptual design requirements and layouts following Design Process Management (DPM) protocols Creating detail, fabrication, and assembly drawings in accordance with ASME Y14.5 standards Modifying and creating 3D models and drawings to manufacturing standards using parametric design practices Supporting manufacturing through application of design‑for‑manufacture principles for machining, welding, and assembly Creating Bills of Materials (BOMs) within documentation systems for engineer approval Participating in design verification activities, including tolerance studies, manufacturability reviews, and basic calculations Supporting Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) and Prototype Verification Test (PVT) procedures and documenting results Ensuring design documentation and data are accurately archived in electronic document management systems Identifying opportunities to improve existing products, processes, and procedures in a cost‑effective manner Fuel your passion To be successful in this role you will: Have a BSc or MSc degree in Mechanical or a related engineering discipline Have a basic understanding of engineering design principles, verification processes, and risk assessment Have knowledge of materials, including metals, elastomers, welding, and heat treatment processes Have awareness of relevant industry standards and engineering codes Be conscientious, adaptable, and eager to learn in a structured engineering environment Have strong written and verbal communication skills Be able to work effectively within a team while responding professionally to changing work demands Have familiarity with engineering design tools, calculation software, and PDM/document management systems Work in a way that works for you We recognize that everyone is different and that the way people deliver their best work can vary. This role supports flexible working arrangements aligned with business and operational requirements. Working with us Our people are at the heart of what we do at Baker Hughes. We are committed to creating an inclusive and collaborative environment where employees are supported, developed, and empowered to grow their careers. Working for you For more than a century, Baker Hughes has led the way in energy innovation.
